learn.canDo: Set timeouts as a budget down a call chain, and pass the deadline along so abandoned work stops.
learn.why: A timeout longer than the caller's is wasted load. Deadline propagation is the standard answer to cascading slowness.

learn.canDo: Estimate how retries multiply load in an outage, and combine backoff, jitter and a retry budget to stay safe.
learn.why: Retry storms turn short blips into long outages. Naming the amplification and the budget is a standard resilience answer.
learn.keyIdea: Backoff changes timing; only a cap changes the total.

learn.canDo: Make a non-idempotent API retry-safe with a per-action key, a long enough key lifetime, and atomic reservation.
learn.why: Every client times out sometimes. Without idempotency, a lost response becomes a double charge.
learn.keyIdea: The key belongs to the action, not the attempt.

learn.canDo: Tune a circuit breaker so it sheds a failing dependency quickly without tripping on noise or lingering shut.
learn.why: Breakers keep one dead dependency from tying up every thread. Tuning them is where candidates differ.

learn.canDo: Size separate pools per dependency from calls per second times duration, and show a shared pool failing together.
learn.why: A slow dependency can starve a shared pool and take healthy features with it. Isolation is the fix.
learn.keyIdea: One slow dependency should exhaust only its own pool.

learn.canDo: Choose consistency or availability during a partition for a given kind of data, and name the latency trade-off otherwise.
learn.why: CAP is asked in nearly every distributed systems interview. PACELC is what shows you understand it beyond the slogan.
learn.keyIdea: Partitions are a given; choose C or A, then latency or consistency.

learn.canDo: Compare linearizable, causal and eventual reads by what a user can notice, and pick the cheapest that is enough.
learn.why: Most products need session guarantees, not linearizability. Knowing the ladder lets you avoid both over- and under-paying.
learn.keyIdea: Guarantee only what a user can notice.

learn.canDo: Explain why wall clocks misorder writes, and choose logical, hybrid, bounded or vector clocks for the need.
learn.why: Last-writer-wins by timestamp silently loses data. Clock questions come up in every replicated-database design.

learn.canDo: Explain Raft's election and majority commit, and tune the election timeout against needless elections and slow failover.
learn.why: Raft underlies etcd, Consul and many databases. Interviewers ask how it elects a leader and what the timers do.

learn.canDo: Explain why a lease can expire under a paused holder, and protect a resource with fencing tokens.
learn.why: Distributed locks look simple and fail in subtle ways. Fencing is the answer that distinguishes careful designs.
learn.keyIdea: Enforce at the point of effect.

learn.canDo: Choose between two-phase commit and a saga for a cross-service workflow, and make the saga's steps and compensations safe to retry.
learn.why: Microservices cannot share a transaction. Sagas are the standard answer, and their weaknesses are the follow-up.

learn.canDo: Avoid lost or phantom events with a transactional outbox, and get exactly-once effects from at-least-once delivery.
learn.why: The dual-write problem appears in every event-driven design. The outbox is the pattern interviewers expect.
learn.keyIdea: Put the event in the same transaction as the data.

chapter.story: Pigeon now depends on many services, and the team learns what happens when each of them is slow, wrong or gone.
outcomes: Set timeouts, retries and breakers that contain failures instead of spreading them
Choose consistency and ordering guarantees for a given kind of data
Coordinate across services without distributed locks that lie
chapter.why: Failure in a distributed system is partial, slow and ambiguous. Each tool in this chapter closes one gap, and each also opens another if used carelessly.
chapter.payoff: In an interview you can walk a request through its failures and say what contains each. At work you will read an outage review and see which of these was missing.
